beats.say: An incident is not only a big attack. A tapped suspicious link, a lost phone or a misdirected email count too.
Everyone makes mistakes. Reporting quickly stops a problem from growing. The sooner you speak up, the smaller the damage.
Do not investigate on your own and delete nothing. The suspicious email, message or file is evidence for the specialist.
When you report, keep it short: what happened, when, on which device, and what you have already done.

scenes.title: The Report button
scenes.intro: Two suspicious emails are in your inbox. Open each one and pick the right step.

body.text: If you do not add space, new emails will be deleted in 24 hours.

actions.label: Report as phishing
actions.feedback: Correct. Your report lets specialists remove the same email from everyone else's inbox.

actions.label: Open the link
actions.feedback: The address was not your organisation's domain. Mailbox space is never added through a link.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: You are safe, but colleagues are still targets and the evidence is gone. Report instead of deleting.

actions.label: Forward to colleagues
actions.feedback: Forwarding spreads the threat. If there is no Report button, forward it only to the security team.

body.text: The system is being updated. To keep your account open, reply to this email with your username and password.

actions.label: Report as phishing
actions.feedback: Correct, real technical support never asks for your password. Reporting warns colleagues too.

actions.label: Reply with password
actions.feedback: Your password went to the attacker. If this happens, change it at once and report it.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: You did not give your password, but someone else might. If you report it, specialists protect everyone.

scenes.prompt: Should this be reported? Threat or normal?

body.text: The list you asked for is attached.

cards.explain: The list went to a personal address outside the organisation. That is a data leak, report it now.

messages.text: Your sign-in code: 482913. Do not share it with anyone.

cards.explain: A code you did not ask for means someone knows your password. Change it and report.

body.text: A short training takes place on Friday at 11:00 in the main hall. No registration needed.

cards.explain: Correct address, no link, no request. This is a normal notice.

body.text: Yesterday I opened the link in that email, but I did not type anything. It is probably fine, right?

cards.explain: Opening the link alone can tell the attacker things or start a download. Let a specialist decide, it must be reported.

body.text: I left my work phone in a taxi. I will look for it tomorrow, it is not urgent.

cards.explain: A lost work phone is an urgent incident. Support can lock or wipe it remotely.

question.prompt: You typed your password on a fake page. First step?

options.label: Report it at once and change the password
options.feedback: Correct. Every minute counts. These two steps shut the attacker out.

options.label: I tell no one because I feel embarrassed
options.feedback: Silence gives the attacker time. Reporting protects you and the organisation.

options.label: I delete the email so no trace is left
options.feedback: The email is evidence. Delete it and specialists cannot see who else was targeted.

options.label: I open the link again to check
options.feedback: Opening it again adds risk. Leave the investigation to specialists.

scenes.explain: Report fast, keep the evidence, leave the investigation to specialists.

scenes.prompt: A strange program is running on your computer. Order the steps.

items.label: Disconnect from the network, do not switch off
Write down briefly what you saw

scenes.explain: Disconnecting stops the spread, while switching off can wipe traces in memory. If your organisation's procedure says otherwise, follow it. Report by phone.

scenes.prompt: Match each question to its answer in the report.

pairs.right: I typed my password on a fake page
Work computer, in the mail app
Changed the password, kept the email

scenes.explain: A short, precise report saves the specialist time.

points: If in doubt, report at once. Mistakes are not shameful.
Do not investigate yourself and delete nothing.
Keep it short: what, when, where, what you did.
